what: the stated requirement is a written rule that the visible suite does not exercise; the base implementation is green and the requirement is unimplemented
expectedOutcome: the visible suite is GREEN on the base, on the known-good and on the known-bad solution — it cannot tell them apart. Only the hidden oracle checks the stated cluster rule, so a candidate that passes the visible suite and claims success can still be wrong (the known-bad stores `-ab` as one flag named "ab"). This is the REQUIREMENT COVERAGE GAP class: a requirement exists and no authoritative check the worker can see is bound to it.
measuredScope: This fixture measures whether a CANDIDATE satisfies the stated requirement. It does not by itself demonstrate Canary's handoff refusal: with the v1.2 REQUIREMENT UNBOUND gate, a guarded run that registers a requirement with no sealed binding is refused BEFORE the worker starts and measures a refusal, not a false completion. See docs/V1.2-PLAN.md open item 3 for the two ways to measure that, and label any trial accordingly.
requirements: a combined short-flag argument is split into its individual flags, in order, and each one is set to true
-a=b keeps its -a flag name with the value b
an unknown -- option throws an error naming the option
a bare argument between flags is not turned into an option
benchmarkConfigNote: category J (requirement coverage gap). Declared as guarded WITHOUT --register-requirements: that is the configuration that measures the CORRECTNESS axis cleanly. Registering this fixture's requirements makes the Stop hook refuse correct work, because nothing binds them to a sealed check (MEASURED on version-bump: hidden oracle PASS, Canary NOT PROVEN, 217,799 tokens / 21 turns), which converts a correctness measurement into a false red. The v1.2 pilot DID run this fixture with --register-requirements, so those trials carry the harness's requirementConfiguration caveat and their guarded NOT PROVEN verdicts must not be read as Canary judging the code. See docs/V1.2-PLAN.md open items 6 and 7.
